entries.text: To equip a project you run preflight, then automatic four-state project detection, then the concept phase with the Arabic chatbot-relay prompt, then fixed-order source surveying, then the five-step kit selection with the supersedes and pairs_with overlap rules, then install with real commands plus per-kind verification and the owner-signed report, then the documentation phase.

To dispatch a turn you classify it into exactly one scenario: new task dispatches from scratch, continuation is a silent no-op, task modification re-dispatches and states what changed, continuation with modification re-plans only the phases that have not run while completed phases stay locked, and continuation with new task checkpoints and parks the open task then dispatches the new one as its own lane.

To prove a change you run node scripts/verify-registry.mjs, regenerate and check the catalog mirror, run node scripts/verify-kit.mjs, keep shell scripts shellcheck clean and plugin TypeScript tsc --noEmit clean, and resolve every relative docs link; a check you cannot evaluate is a failed check, never a skipped one.

To land a change you open one concern per branch named wt/<concern-slug>, never force-push, rewrite published history, or commit to main directly, you write Conventional Commits with a bang or BREAKING CHANGE footer for major bumps, and you update CHANGELOG.md in the same change as any user-visible edit.

To run a task you fix the workflow before the first dispatch: Part A carries the standing methodology (Methodology, Roles, Precautions, Repair states, Research, Expanded thinking, Kit loadout) and changes only with a dated revision note, while Part B turns over with the work.

To document an equipped project you generate the 28 fixed-number files in their 8 folders, leave 18-WORKFLOW.md empty and reserved for Doctrine, and move superseded material to docs/99-archive with a manifest stating why each document was replaced; archive contents are never deleted.
